messages:
Maria: spinning up a kubeadm cluster in ap-south2 for the new inference edge pool (3 control, 6 GPU workers). hitting subnet overlap with our shared-prod-vpc, need quick plan.
Samir: did you pick /20 or /21 for the cluster?
Maria: default cloud template tried allocating /20 (10.44.0.0/20) which conflicts with prod's 10.44.0.0/21.
Jia: we should avoid re-IPing prod. easiest is pick a non-overlapping pod range and set Calico IP pool accordingly.
Kevin: networking note: the region's default VPC CIDR space is tight. if we move cluster to a new subnet we may need to request additional CIDR from cloud team — that takes ~2-4h.
Maria: timeline: want to finish bootstrap and smoke by EOD. can we do a local workaround (node-local routes) and then request CIDR?
Samir: yes — temporary approach: set Calico to use 192.168.0.0/18 for pods (cluster-internal) and enable IPIP encapsulation. avoids touching VPC. add these to kubeadm config before init.
Maria: sample kubeadm snippets I used: ```yaml
networking:
  podSubnet: 192.168.0.0/18
  serviceSubnet: 10.96.0.0/12
```
Samir: also update calicoctl ippool: ```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: IPPool
metadata:
  name: redwood-edge-pool
spec:
  cidr: 192.168.0.0/18
  ipipMode: Always
  natOutgoing: true
  disabled: false
```
Kevin: remember to set MTU on the pod iface to 1400 if underlying ENI MTU=9000 and IPIP adds overhead. otherwise large payloads will fragment.
Alex: on call checklist: mark GPU nodes with taint `nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule` then add tolerations to inference daemonsets. also label nodes with `region=ap-south2` and `pool=edge-gpu-rtx` for placement.
Maria: commands I ran for node labels/tolerations: ```bash
kubectl label nodes gpu-worker-1 region=ap-south2 pool=edge-gpu-rtx
kubectl taint nodes gpu-worker-1 nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule-
``` (remove taint to allow scheduling for our test pods)
Jia: small gotcha — kube-proxy in ipvs mode needs conntrack_max tuned for high concurrent streams from inferencing; we bumped to 262144 in sysctl for other clusters. add to node daemonset config.
Samir: cost note: these GPU workers are spot instances to save ~$65% but we need a fallback on preemptions: set node-pool auto-replace with warm on-demand standby 1 instance.
Maria: deploy-bot: rolling deploy started for calico manifest v1.2.3 to the new cluster.
deploy-bot: [notice] rollout initiated by Maria at 2026-03-18T15:18:10Z
Kevin: final validation checklist before handoff to SRE: 1) control plane healthy 2) calico pods all running 3) kube-proxy ipvs running 4) mtus validated 5) GPU drivers + nvidia-device-plugin OK 6) network egress for APT/OS updates allowed
Maria: status after smoke: control plane ok, calico 3/3 running, nv drivers installed on 5/6 workers (one failed driver dkms build), ipvs active, MTU 1400 on pods.
Jia: action: open ticket for the driver fail (probably kernel mismatch). tag infra-ops and cc Kevin.
Samir: also add a note in runbook: temporary podCIDR workaround used, must re-IP or request VPC CIDR before we promote cluster to Dedicated.
Maria: will create handoff message once driver and CIDR ticket are resolved. thanks all :thumbsup:
